hitl_conditions: Allocation of control blocks (Fig. 8) to human, automation or AI is configurable by degree of human-AI collaboration; decision rights follow who holds the most complete information; humans keep non-standardized situations and verify AI outputs against hallucination.
key_finding: Theory-building paper: defines the digital supply chain ecosystem, formalizes the twin as a control-theoretic decision-support loop (plan, control, observe, adapt) and a cyber-physical framework with a human-AI collaboration space; AI generates/adapts models and scenarios and recommends actions, while humans verify and decide (AI agent is support, not decision-maker).

HITL evidence: Section 2.1 (Fig. 1 three DT levels by degree of human-AI collaboration; Fig. 2 areas of human-AI collaboration: AI for standardized tasks, humans for non-standardized situations, delegation, AI enhances human metaknowledge; hallucination paragraph: 'human-in-the-loop oversight' and explainable AI); Section 3, paragraph after Eq. 6 (which Fig. 8 blocks are controlled by a human, automatically, or AI-driven is left configurable; the 'subject (decision-maker)' owns the control vector u(t) and correction actions v(x(t),t)); Section 5.1 (procedure: 'Supplemented by human knowledge, verification and assessment take place leading to the recognition and control of the physical supply chain'); Section 5.3 (CERERE Cognitive Human Interface & Governance: human-in-the-loop + reinforcement learning with human feedback + explainable AI; INC 'recommend next-best action', 'automated workflows'); Section 6, last two paragraphs (decision allocation by who has the most complete information; 'An AI agent is a decision-making support, not a decision-maker'). quotes.text: we outline a generalized framework of the cyber-physical supply chain comprised of a digital ecosystem, digital twin, human-AI collaboration space, and the physical supply chain

A digital ecosystem is a set of digital technologies, AI-based knowledge management systems, cloud spaces, and platforms that encapsulate supply chain data enabling digital twins and simulation models.

Different degrees of human-AI collaboration can define which blocks in Fig. 8 are controlled by a human, what is controlled/adjusted automatically, what is AI-driven, and where a human-AI collaboration takes place.
quotes.section: 3. Generalized models of digital twinning in the supply chain (paragraph after Eq. 6, before Fig. 9)

quotes.text: human-in-the-loop approaches coupled with reinforcement learning to embed human feedback into the recommendation engine and explainable AI methods will be adopted.
quotes.section: 5.3 Application scenario 2: supply chain collaboration (Cognitive Human Interface & Governance, CERERE)

quotes.text: Depending on who has the most complete information about a physical object – an AI agent in a digital twin or a human in the physical space, decision-making can be performed in a human-AI collaboration fashion.

the importance of combining expert knowledge and AI should be strengthened to avoid automatic decisions based on wrong AI recommendations. An AI agent is a decision-making support, not a decision-maker.
quotes.section: 6. Discussion and conclusion (last paragraph, barriers: AI hallucination)
